facts.claim: Wilsons Promontory is the southernmost point of the Australian mainland; South Point is its tip.
The park covers about 50,000 hectares with about 130 km of walking trails and a number of campsites.
Tidal River is the hub and the only settlement in the park, with a store, visitor centre and camping.
Wombats are common around the campsites and the wildlife there is used to people.
The Wilsons Promontory Lighthouse stands at South East Point.

experiences: Walk to granite peaks and coastal views
Swim and stroll on white-sand beaches
Meet wombats at the campsites
Hike or camp at the southern tip of the mainland

tips.title: Book overnight hikes
tips.detail: Permits are required for overnight hikes and can be booked ahead or on arrival at the park entrance or Tidal River visitor centre.

tips.title: Long drive to the hub
tips.detail: Tidal River is about 30 km inside the park entrance, so allow time for the drive in.

tips.title: Secure your food
tips.detail: Wombats and birds around Tidal River's campsites approach people and have entered tents looking for food.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (southern summer to early autumn for beaches and long hikes); no source read gives months.

name: Wilsons Promontory National Park

facts.claim: Grampians National Park (Gariwerd) covers 167,219 hectares between Stawell, Horsham and Dunkeld, about 260 km west of Melbourne.
It is on the National Heritage List for its natural beauty and as one of the richest Aboriginal rock art sites in south-eastern Australia.
The Gariwerd area holds about 90 per cent of the rock art in Victoria.
The ranges are renowned for hiking trails, wildlife and wildflowers.
Halls Gap is the only town and main access point; kangaroos feed across the road from the Halls Gap supermarket in the late afternoon.

experiences: Hike sandstone ranges to lookouts
See Aboriginal rock art at Gariwerd
Chase waterfalls and wildflowers
Watch kangaroos graze at Halls Gap

tips.title: Start at Brambuk
tips.detail: The Brambuk National Park and Cultural Centre in Halls Gap has displays on the park and its Aboriginal culture.

tips.title: Dusk wildlife
tips.detail: Kangaroos come to feed in the late afternoon on the grass across from the Halls Gap supermarket.

tips.title: Two ways in
tips.detail: Halls Gap is the main access, with Dunkeld a quieter southern gateway below Mount Abrupt and Mount Sturgeon.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED (spring wildflowers and mild autumn); the page names wildflowers but no months.

name: Grampians National Park

facts.claim: Port Campbell National Park is a 1,750-hectare park on the Shipwreck Coast about 190 km south-west of Melbourne.
It protects limestone cliffs, rock stacks, gorges, arches and blowholes and was dedicated in 1964.
Its attractions include the Twelve Apostles, London Bridge, Loch Ard Gorge, the Gibson Steps and The Grotto.
The stacks formed as Southern Ocean weather eroded soft limestone into caves, then arches that collapsed.
There are no park fees or permits, though there may be parking fees.

experiences: See the Twelve Apostles' limestone stacks
Walk down to beaches and gorges
Watch sunset on the Shipwreck Coast
Look for penguins at dusk

tips.title: Allow for the drive
tips.detail: Melbourne to the Twelve Apostles can take up to 5 hours on the Great Ocean Road.

tips.title: Entry is free
tips.detail: The park has no entry fee or permits, though car parks may charge.

tips.title: Penguins at dusk
tips.detail: Penguins are best seen in summer, just after sunset.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (penguins best in summer per the page; the coast is windier in winter).

name: Port Campbell National Park

facts.claim: Melbourne is Victoria's capital and Australia's second most populous city, with about 5.4 million people as of June 2025.
It sits on the northern and eastern shores of Port Phillip Bay and is claimed to be the southernmost city in the world with over a million people.
It hosts the Australian Grand Prix and the Australian Open and held the 1956 Summer Olympics.
It is described as the cultural capital of Australia, with many galleries, a live music scene and a strong food, wine and coffee culture.
It is a base for day trips to the Grampians, the Great Ocean Road and Phillip Island.

experiences: Wander laneways, cafes and street art
Catch live sport at the MCG
Browse galleries and museums
Eat across the world's cuisines

tips.title: Free tram zone
tips.detail: Trams within the CBD's Free Tram Zone need no touch-on, but touching on there charges a fare.

tips.title: Four seasons in a day
tips.detail: The climate is notorious for its changeability, so carry a layer even on a warm day.

tips.title: Get a myki
tips.detail: Public transport runs on a myki card (adult card $6), a mobile myki or a Visa or Mastercard.

best_months.rationale: Summer (Dec-Feb) averages around 26C by day and October is typically the wettest month.

seasonal_tags: Melbourne Cup first Tuesday of November
name: Melbourne

facts.claim: Croajingolong National Park is an 88,355-hectare coastal park in East Gippsland, about 450 km east of Melbourne.
The name comes from Krauatungalung words meaning 'belonging to the east'.
Its landscape ranges from rocky outcrops, sandy beaches and dunes to rivers, and UNESCO nominated it a World Biosphere Reserve in 1977.
The Wilderness Coast Walk runs 45 km from Thurra River camping area to Shipwreck Creek.
Popular places include Point Hicks and its lighthouse, Thurra River sand dunes, Wingan Inlet and Mount Everard.
The only town of any size is Mallacoota; entry has no fee.

experiences: Hike the remote Wilderness Coast
Camp beside quiet inlets and beaches
Paddle and fish at Mallacoota

tips.title: Walk permit
tips.detail: A permit from Parks Victoria is needed before attempting the Wilderness Coast Walk.

tips.title: Bring your food
tips.detail: Outside Mallacoota there are no places to eat in the park, so pack your own supplies.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer and early autumn for camping and swimming).

name: Croajingolong National Park

facts.claim: Ararat is a town about 198 km west of Melbourne on the Western Highway, between the Western District and the Wimmera.
Gold was discovered in 1857 and turned it into a boomtown, and it is the only city in Australia founded by Chinese people.
It is known as the Gateway to the Grampians and its area is becoming known for wine.
Things to see include J Ward, the former home of the criminally insane, the Gum San Chinese heritage museum, and the One Tree Hill and Flint Hill lookouts.
V/Line trains run from Melbourne's Southern Cross Station three times daily on weekdays.

experiences: Tour Ararat's Chinese gold-rush heritage
Taste cool-climate wine

tips.title: Train from Melbourne
tips.detail: V/Line trains run from Southern Cross Station three times daily on weekdays and twice daily on weekends.

tips.title: Grampians gateway
tips.detail: Ararat is billed as the gateway to the Grampians, with Halls Gap reached by V/Line bus.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (mild spring and autumn).

wikivoyage_page: redirect: "Ararat" is a disambiguation page; the town page is https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Ararat_(Victoria)
name: Ararat

facts.claim: Warrnambool is a city of 32,894 people (2021) on the south-west coast of Victoria and marks the western end of the Great Ocean Road.
The name comes from Mount Warrnambool, a scoria cone volcano 25 km north-east of the town.
Southern right whales can be seen from the Logans Beach platform between June and September.
Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum is a headline attraction, with a night-time 'Shipwrecked' show about the Loch Ard wreck.
The traditional owners are the Dhauwurd Wurrung people, also known as the Gunditjmara.

experiences: Watch southern right whales from shore
Explore maritime history and shipwreck stories
Use it as a base for the Shipwreck Coast

tips.title: Whale season
tips.detail: Southern right whales are seen from the Logans Beach platform between June and September, often without binoculars.

tips.title: Road's western end
tips.detail: Warrnambool marks the western end of the Great Ocean Road, with some travellers continuing on to Port Fairy.

best_months.rationale: Southern right whales can be seen from Logans Beach between June and September.

name: Warrnambool

facts.claim: The Mornington Peninsula lies south-east of Melbourne between Port Phillip, Western Port and Bass Strait, ending at Point Nepean.
About 163,847 people lived there in 2017, rising to 225,000-250,000 in peak summer, making it Victoria's most populous coastal holiday area.
The highest point, Arthurs Seat, is 305 metres above sea level and unusually close to the shore.
Red Hill is known for rolling green hills, wineries, fresh produce and a community market.
The first European settlement in Victoria was at what is now Sorrento; Prime Minister Harold Holt disappeared while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967.

experiences: Taste wine and produce at Red Hill
Swim and surf at the beaches
Walk the national park at Point Nepean

tips.title: Wineries and mazes
tips.detail: Popular attractions are the wineries, mazes and water sports on Port Phillip and Western Port.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: The peninsula's population jumps to 225,000-250,000 at peak summer, so expect crowds at beaches and on roads.

tips.title: Use the right beach
tips.detail: Calm Port Phillip beaches suit swimming while surf breaks such as Portsea back beach face Bass Strait.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (beach season); the page notes summer peak crowds.

name: Mornington Peninsula

facts.claim: The Gippsland Lakes are a network of coastal lakes, marshes and lagoons of about 354 sq km between Lakes Entrance, Bairnsdale and Sale.
The largest lakes are Lake Wellington, Lake King and Lake Victoria.
Sea currents formed Ninety Mile Beach, which cut off the river deltas from the sea.
A 1889 wall fixed the channel to the ocean at Lakes Entrance, creating a harbour for fishing boats.
Lakes Entrance is a popular coastal destination at the mouth of the lakes, and Paynesville is a boating resort.

experiences: Cruise and kayak the lakes
Paddle among lakeside towns
Walk the long sands of Ninety Mile Beach

tips.title: Boating hubs
tips.detail: Paynesville is a boating resort and Lakes Entrance sits at the lakes' mouth, both good bases for time on the water.

tips.title: Train to Bairnsdale
tips.detail: V/Line trains run east only as far as Bairnsdale, so reach Lakes Entrance and beyond by coach or car.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer boating); no source read gives months. Wikivoyage has no Gippsland Lakes page.

wikivoyage_page: no (Wikivoyage Gippsland Lakes is missing; East Gippsland and Lakes Entrance pages exist: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/East_Gippsland)
name: Gippsland Lakes

facts.claim: Hamilton is a city in south-western Victoria at the junction of the Glenelg and Henty Highways, linked to Geelong by the Hamilton Highway.
It claims to be the 'Wool Capital of the World' from its history of sheep grazing.
Hamilton Botanic Gardens were designed by William Guilfoyle in 1881 and have rare plants, a restored rotunda and a small zoo.
The Sir Reginald Ansett Transport Museum displays the airline's first aircraft, a Fokker Universal.

experiences: Visit wool-country heritage museums
Stroll Guilfoyle-designed botanic gardens

tips.title: Visitor centre
tips.detail: The Visitor Information Centre is at 86 Hamilton Place.

tips.title: Grampians next
tips.detail: The Grampians are a short drive away, which makes Hamilton a stop on the way.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Hamilton (Victoria)

facts.claim: Portland is the oldest European settlement in Victoria, on Portland Bay, with a population of 10,016 (2021).
More than 200 historical buildings from the 1800s survive.
The Maritime Discovery Centre shows its sealing and whaling past, with a sperm whale skeleton and shipwreck displays.
The 250 km Great South West Walk begins at the Portland Visitor Information Centre.
Whales often visit in the winter months.

experiences: Walk the Great South West Walk
Discover Victoria's oldest settlement

tips.title: Limited transport
tips.detail: A V/Line train and coach link goes via Warrnambool; there is no regular passenger air service.

tips.title: Winter whales
tips.detail: Whales often visit Portland Bay in the winter months.

best_months.rationale: Whales often visit in the winter months (source gives no months).

name: Portland

facts.claim: Phillip Island is 26 km long and 9 km wide, about 125 km south-south-east of Melbourne, joined to the mainland by a 640 m bridge from San Remo.
Its Penguin Parade at Summerland Beach is the signature attraction, with around 40,000 little penguins on the island.
Seal Rocks off the western end hosts Australia's largest colony of fur seals.
The Koala Conservation Centre has two tree-top boardwalks for close views of koalas.
The island has a motor-racing history, with Australia's first international Grand Prix held there in 1924.
Humpback and southern right whales are seen from The Nobbies as they migrate in winter.

experiences: Watch little penguins come ashore at dusk
See koalas from tree-top boardwalks
Spot fur seals and whales from The Nobbies
Watch motor racing at the Grand Prix circuit

tips.title: No bus to sights
tips.detail: There is no public bus to the Penguin Parade, Rhyll, the Grand Prix Circuit or the Nobbies, so a car is the way around.

tips.title: Event traffic
tips.detail: Melbourne to Cowes is about 2 hours by road and up to 3 hours during major events such as the Grand Prix.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: The island's population swells from about 13,800 to 40,000 in summer.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer; population swells to 40,000 then). Whales pass The Nobbies in winter.

seasonal_tags: MotoGP and Grand Prix round (annual, dates unverified)
name: Phillip Island

facts.claim: South Gippsland is a well-watered region of rolling hills falling to the coast, and includes Wilsons Promontory, the southernmost point of the Australian mainland.
The principal towns include Leongatha, Korumburra, Wonthaggi and Foster.
Fish Creek is an eclectic artisanal stop on the way to the Prom and Foster is a base for exploring it.
Tarra-Bulga National Park has a famous suspension bridge walk.
The main visitor centre is the Prom Country Information Centre at Korumburra.

experiences: Drive through Prom Country villages
Walk to the Tarra-Bulga suspension bridge
Surf and fish along the coast

tips.title: Highway route
tips.detail: The South Gippsland Highway leaves the Princes Highway at Dandenong and rejoins it at Sale, passing the main towns.

tips.title: Visitor centre
tips.detail: The Prom Country Information Centre is on the South Gippsland Highway at Korumburra.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer coast).

name: South Gippsland

facts.claim: Horsham is the Wimmera's largest city, about 300 km north-west of Melbourne on a bend in the Wimmera River, with 16,985 people in 2021.
Wheat and wool built the city, and it was named Victoria's Tidiest Town in 2021.
Horsham Regional Art Gallery and Horsham Botanic Gardens are among the listed sights.
Mount Arapiles, one of Australia's most famous rock-climbing areas, is about 30 minutes drive west.

experiences: Stop for Wimmera art and gardens
Climb at nearby Mount Arapiles

tips.title: Highway stopover
tips.detail: The town sits on the Western Highway and is popular as a stopover, about 4 hours from Melbourne.

tips.title: Day trip west
tips.detail: Mount Arapiles is about 30 minutes drive west of Horsham.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Horsham

facts.claim: Mount Buffalo National Park covers 31,000 hectares in the Victorian Alps, about 350 km north-east of Melbourne.
The plateau rises to 1,723 m and is topped by striking granite boulders and rock formations.
Reserved in 1898, it is one of the oldest national parks in Australia.
A walking track climbs The Horn, the highest accessible point, for a 360 degree view.
In winter it is a cross-country skiing destination with toboggan runs at Dingo Dell and Cresta Valley.
Eurobin Falls was part of the original reserve; the Lake Catani camping ground is open November to April.

experiences: Walk granite tors and lookouts
Ski cross-country or toboggan in winter
Camp beside Lake Catani

tips.title: Camping season
tips.detail: The camping ground at Lake Catani is open November to April.

tips.title: Winter on the plateau
tips.detail: In winter the plateau is used for cross-country skiing and toboggan runs.

tips.title: Climb The Horn
tips.detail: A walking track climbs The Horn, the highest accessible point, for a 360 degree view from the top.

best_months.rationale: Camping at Lake Catani runs November to April; winter (Jul-Aug) suits snow play (UNVERIFIED months).

wikivoyage_page: no (Wikivoyage Mount Buffalo and Mount Buffalo National Park are missing)
name: Mount Buffalo National Park

facts.claim: Mildura is a regional city of 35,652 (2021) on the Murray River in Victoria's north-west and the largest settlement in Sunraysia.
About 90 per cent of Australia's table grape exports are grown in the Sunraysia region, and it supplies about 80 per cent of Victoria's grapes.
It was Australia's first irrigation colony and is called an oasis in the desert.
Visitors can cruise the Murray on the paddlesteamer Melbourne or a chartered houseboat, and watch paddle steamers go through the lock and weir.
Mungo National Park is about two hours away and can be seen in a day trip.

experiences: Cruise the Murray on a paddle steamer
Eat and drink at Sunraysia's vineyards
Day-trip to Mungo National Park

tips.title: Summer heat
tips.detail: Summers are hot, averaging 32C by day, with some days over 40C.

tips.title: Far from Melbourne
tips.detail: Melbourne is a 10 hour V/Line bus ride and Adelaide is closer, so fly into Mildura Airport.

best_months.rationale: Summers average a hot 32C with days over 40C and winters 15C, so autumn and spring are milder (UNVERIFIED months).

name: Mildura

facts.claim: Ballarat is Victoria's third-largest city, about 110 km north-west of Melbourne, with 111,973 people in 2021.
Gold was found at Poverty Point on 18 August 1851, and about 20,000 migrants arrived within months.
The Eureka Rebellion of 3 December 1854 took place here, and the Eureka Flag is held at the Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka.
Sovereign Hill turned Ballarat into a major cultural tourist destination.
Lake Wendouree hosted the rowing events of the 1956 Summer Olympics.

experiences: Step into the gold rush at Sovereign Hill
Learn the story of the Eureka Rebellion
Stroll Victorian streets and Lake Wendouree

tips.title: Easy from Melbourne
tips.detail: Ballarat is about 110 km from Melbourne and reachable by train or car for a day trip.

tips.title: Information centre
tips.detail: The Ballarat Information Centre is at 43 Lydiard St North, opposite the art gallery.

tips.title: Eureka sites
tips.detail: The Eureka Flag is held at the Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (mild autumn and spring).

name: Ballarat

facts.claim: Geelong is Victoria's second-largest city, 75 km south-west of Melbourne at the western end of Corio Bay, with about 282,809 people in 2023.
It is the gateway to the Bellarine Peninsula and the Great Ocean Road.
The National Wool Museum and an antique carousel on the waterfront are among its attractions.
The traditional owners are the Wadawurrung people, and the name comes from Djilang.
Geelong boomed in the 1850s as the main port to the goldfields.

experiences: Walk the waterfront and bollards
Learn wool history at the National Wool Museum
Base for the Great Ocean Road

tips.title: Close to Melbourne
tips.detail: Geelong is 75 km from Melbourne and has good transport links to the city and the Great Ocean Road.

tips.title: Beaches and wineries
tips.detail: The city is known for its beaches and nearby wineries.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (waterfront and beach season).

name: Geelong

facts.claim: Alpine National Park is Victoria's largest national park at 646,000 hectares (6,474 sq km), covering much of the Great Dividing Range in the state.
It includes Victoria's highest point, Mount Bogong at 1,986 m, and the Bogong High Plains.
It joins Kosciuszko National Park across the New South Wales border.
Part of the 665 km Australian Alps Walking Track passes through, starting in Walhalla.
There are no towns in the park, but Mount Hotham and Falls Creek ski resorts sit among it.

experiences: Hike the high plains and peaks
Ski at Mount Hotham and Falls Creek
Walk part of the Australian Alps Walking Track
Chase waterfalls such as Paradise Falls

tips.title: Resorts are the bases
tips.detail: No towns lie in the park; the main entrances are by Falls Creek and Mount Hotham.

tips.title: Paradise Falls road
tips.detail: The 31 m Paradise Falls near Cheshunt needs 11 km on unsealed road, and flows best in spring or early summer.

tips.title: Long-distance track
tips.detail: Part of the 665 km Australian Alps Walking Track passes through the park, starting in Walhalla and ending near Canberra.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED (summer walking and winter snow for the ski resorts).

name: Alpine National Park

facts.claim: Echuca is a Murray River port town (15,056 people in 2021) at the closest point of the Murray to Melbourne, near the Goulburn, Campaspe and Murray junction.
The name is a Yorta Yorta word meaning meeting of the waters.
It became a thriving 19th-century river port, and paddle steamers unloaded at the 332 m red gum Echuca Wharf.
It was founded by ex-convict Henry Hopwood, whose ferry gave the town its start.
Things to do include riverboat cruises, water sports and eco tours; Moama is the twin town across the river.

experiences: Cruise the Murray on riverboats
See the red gum wharf of a river port
Cross to twin town Moama

tips.title: Reach by coach
tips.detail: Coaches from Melbourne take 2 hr 45 min; the train detours through Bendigo and takes about 3 hours.

tips.title: Few buses
tips.detail: Apart from occasional buses there is little transport around town, so walk or drive.

tips.title: Seat tip
tips.detail: On the Echuca train sit in the front three cars, as the rear three decouple at Bendigo.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (warm river season).

name: Echuca

facts.claim: Bendigo is Victoria's fourth-largest city, about 150 km north-west of Melbourne, with an urban population of 103,818 in 2022.
Gold was discovered on Bendigo Creek in 1851, funding the grand Victorian architecture in the city centre.
The Dja Dja Wurrung (Djaara) are the traditional owners.
A tram network began in 1890 and a tourist hop-on hop-off tram runs the main street.
Poppet Head Lookout and Bendigo Art Gallery are a short walk from the park.

experiences: Admire gold-rush architecture
Ride the heritage tram
Explore art and Chinese heritage

tips.title: Easy from Melbourne
tips.detail: Bendigo is about 1.5 hours' drive from Melbourne and on a train line from Southern Cross Station.

tips.title: Tourist tram
tips.detail: A hop-on hop-off tram runs up and down the main street.

tips.title: Gold history
tips.detail: Chinese settlers formed a large part of the gold-rush population; look for the heritage in the city.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Bendigo

facts.claim: The Bellarine Peninsula lies south-west of Melbourne between Port Phillip, Corio Bay and Bass Strait, with about 70,000 residents, doubling at peak periods in summer.
It began as a wheat and grain area before becoming a tourist destination, with most visitors arriving by paddle steamer in the late 19th century.
Today it is known for beaches, seaside resorts and wineries.
Queenscliff has shops and restaurants and a ferry terminal with a service to the Mornington Peninsula.
Portarlington is a historic coastal town busy in summer, and Barwon Heads sits at the Barwon River mouth.

experiences: Taste wine and produce on the peninsula
Swim at family beaches
Ferry across the bay from Queenscliff

tips.title: Bay ferry
tips.detail: A ferry from Queenscliff crosses to the Mornington Peninsula.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: The population doubles at peak periods in summer, particularly at Portarlington.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer beach season; population doubles then).

name: Bellarine Peninsula

facts.claim: Mansfield is a town in the foothills of the Victorian Alps, about 180 km north-east of Melbourne, with 5,541 people in 2021.
It is the support town for the Mount Buller ski resort.
It is linked to the high-country tradition celebrated in The Man from Snowy River, with a film made near Craigs Hut.
Lake Eildon and Lake Nillahcootie are close, and summer waterskiing is popular.
Activities include skiing at Mount Buller and Mount Stirling, horse riding, mountain biking, fishing and white water rafting.

experiences: Ride horses through the high country
Ski Mount Buller in winter
Water-ski on Lake Eildon

tips.title: Drive from Melbourne
tips.detail: The drive from Melbourne is about two hours via the Yarra Valley and the B300.

tips.title: Visitor centre
tips.detail: The Mansfield Visitor Information Centre is at 175 High Street.

best_months.rationale: Skiing at Mount Buller in winter and lake water sports in summer (UNVERIFIED months).

name: Mansfield

facts.claim: The Dandenong Ranges lie about 35 km east of Melbourne and rise to 633 m at Mount Dandenong, topped by TV towers.
Four chunks of the ranges form the Dandenong Ranges National Park.
The ranges are covered in temperate rainforest of tall mountain ash and ferny undergrowth, and have been popular with day-trippers since the 1870s.
The valley between the hills has the towns of Olinda, Sassafras and Kallista.
Puffing Billy leaves from near Belgrave station on the Belgrave line.

experiences: Walk fern gullies and mountain ash
Ride Puffing Billy through the hills
Browse the Olinda and Sassafras villages

tips.title: Train from Melbourne
tips.detail: Belgrave line trains reach the ranges in just over an hour; Puffing Billy leaves from near Belgrave.

tips.title: Sunday buses
tips.detail: Ventura bus 688 from Croydon is infrequent but the only Sunday service to Mount Dandenong and Olinda.

tips.title: Not Dandenong suburb
tips.detail: The suburb of Dandenong is 30 km from the mountain of the same name, so check the destination.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (cool, green autumn and spring).

name: Dandenong Ranges

facts.claim: Daylesford is a former gold-mining town (founded 1852) about 114 km north-west of Melbourne, with 2,781 people in 2021.
It is one of Australia's few spa towns, and the area including Hepburn Springs holds over 80 per cent of the country's effervescent mineral water reserve.
Daylesford has the highest concentration of natural mineral springs in Australia.
Sights include the Convent Gallery, Stony Creek Gallery and Lake Daylesford, a popular spot to walk and picnic.
The town is small and walkable, but sights outside it need a car or bike.

experiences: Soak in mineral spas
Wander galleries, gardens and lakeside paths
Eat and drink at country restaurants

tips.title: Car for outlying sights
tips.detail: The town is walkable but sights outside it need a car or bike, and the steep streets make cycling hard.

tips.title: Few coach stops
tips.detail: V/Line coaches come from Castlemaine, Ballarat or Woodend and stop only once in Daylesford.

tips.title: Spa town
tips.detail: Daylesford and Hepburn Springs are spa towns with natural mineral springs.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (cool-season spa stays); no source read gives months.

name: Daylesford

facts.claim: The Surf Coast Shire covers 1,553 sq km south-west of Geelong and includes the coastal towns of Torquay, Anglesea, Aireys Inlet and Lorne.
The Great Ocean Road starts at Torquay and runs west, hugging the coast known east of the Otways as the Surf Coast.
Bells Beach hosts the world's longest-running pro surfing competition, the Rip Curl Pro, held at Easter since 1962.
Torquay is home to Rip Curl and Quiksilver and to the Australian National Surfing Museum.
The Great Ocean Road was built by returned soldiers between 1919 and 1932 and is called the world's largest war memorial.

experiences: Surf the breaks at Bells Beach
Drive the start of the Great Ocean Road
Visit the Australian National Surfing Museum

tips.title: Surf competition
tips.detail: Bells Beach's Rip Curl Pro has been held every Easter since 1962, apart from occasional venue changes when conditions are poor.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: Torquay's population usually triples between January and February.

tips.title: Windy road
tips.detail: The Great Ocean Road can get very windy in parts, and climate is a few degrees cooler than Melbourne.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer beach season); Torquay's population triples Jan-Feb. Easter surfing event is a yearly pattern.

wikivoyage_page: no (Wikivoyage "Surf Coast" is missing; "Great Ocean Road" page exists: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Great_Ocean_Road)
name: Surf Coast

facts.claim: Bright is a town of 2,620 people (2021) at the south-eastern end of the Ovens Valley in north-eastern Victoria, 319 m above sea level.
Gold was found in the 1850s, the Ovens River was dredged clean by the 1950s and tourism had already begun.
Autumn visitors come to view the changing colours of European trees planted in the area.
Cyclists come for the trails and motorcyclists for the Great Alpine Road, and it is the gateway to alpine scenery and winter skiing.
Beechworth and Mount Hotham are the suggested next stops.

experiences: See autumn colour along the Ovens River
Ride the trails and the Great Alpine Road
Swim and paddle the Ovens in summer

tips.title: Autumn colour
tips.detail: European trees planted in the valley change colour in autumn, drawing visitors.

tips.title: Long drive
tips.detail: Bright is about 3.5 hours from Melbourne and 1.5 hours from Albury-Wodonga, and nearly everyone arrives by road.

tips.title: Summer swimming
tips.detail: In spring and summer there is swimming and water sports on the Ovens River.

best_months.rationale: Autumn for foliage; spring and summer for river swimming (months UNVERIFIED).

name: Bright

facts.claim: The Yarra Valley is a wine region around the Yarra River, about an hour's drive from Melbourne, with more than 80 wineries.
Its cool climate suits Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.
The valley runs from forested ranges near the river's source down to flatter farmland and vineyards.
The Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail runs through the valley.
Healesville, Warburton, Yarra Glen and Kinglake are the valley's main towns.

experiences: Taste cool-climate wine at cellar doors
Ride or walk the rail trail
See wildlife and mountain forests

tips.title: Wineries on the highway
tips.detail: Many of the 80-plus wineries are signposted along the Maroondah Highway through the valley centre.

tips.title: Drive if tasting
tips.detail: Wineries are spread along the valley, so arrange a driver or tour if you plan to taste.

tips.title: Rail trail
tips.detail: The Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail suits a gentler day on foot or bike.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (autumn harvest and spring); no source read gives months.

name: Yarra Valley

facts.claim: The Macedon Ranges is a Central Victorian region between Melbourne and Bendigo, known for native forests, arts, food and wine, and weekly farmers' markets.
Hanging Rock and Mount Macedon are its best-known natural attractions.
The 1975 film Picnic at Hanging Rock, directed by Peter Weir, made Hanging Rock famous.
It has more working artists per capita than anywhere else in Victoria.
Towns include Kyneton, Woodend, Gisborne, Lancefield and Romsey.

experiences: Climb Hanging Rock's volcanic outcrops
Drive up Mount Macedon
Browse country towns and markets

tips.title: Day trip
tips.detail: Everything in the Goldfields is roughly a 60-minute scenic trip from everything else, and the region is best explored by car.

tips.title: Wineries nearby
tips.detail: The region has a large number of wineries and vineyards.

tips.title: Hanging Rock info
tips.detail: Hanging Rock Recreation Reserve has a ranger line on +61 418 373 032.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Macedon Ranges

facts.claim: Lorne is a town of 1,327 people (2021) in Surf Coast Shire on Louttit Bay and the Erskine River.
It was named in 1871 after the Marquess of Lorne, and the Great Ocean Road reached it in 1922.
The Great Ocean Road was officially opened near the Grand Pacific Hotel in Lorne in November 1932.
Rudyard Kipling visited in 1891 and was inspired to write the poem The Flowers.
Lorne's beach runs about 3 km and there is Teddy's Lookout and Great Otway National Park nearby.

experiences: Swim and surf the long bay beach
Walk to waterfalls in the Otways
Drive the Great Ocean Road to Teddys Lookout

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: Holiday-makers fill the town to bursting every summer.

tips.title: Two hours from Melbourne
tips.detail: Lorne is about two hours from Melbourne along the Great Ocean Road.

tips.title: Steep roads to the lookout
tips.detail: Drive carefully on the steep roads up to Teddy's Lookout.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement; the page says summer fills the town.

name: Lorne

facts.claim: Beechworth is a gold-rush town of 3,290 people (2021) in north-east Victoria's High Country.
Its well-preserved historic precinct includes the Court House and the Burke Museum, and Beechworth is associated with bushranger Ned Kelly.
The old railway line to Wangaratta and to Bright has been converted to a paved rail trail with a downhill ride from Beechworth.
It has become a wine-producing centre and popular tourist destination.
Beechworth Honey offers a retail outlet and tour on beekeeping, and Newtown Falls is a natural sight.

experiences: Walk gold-rush streets and historic buildings
Ride the rail trail downhill
Taste honey and local produce

tips.title: Car or foot
tips.detail: There is no car hire in Beechworth, so bring your own vehicle or walk.

tips.title: Bike hire
tips.detail: Bicycles can be hired in town for the rail trail, including a day ride to Everton for lunch.

tips.title: Visitor centre
tips.detail: The Visitor Information Centre is at 103 Ford Street.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Beechworth

facts.claim: Yarra Ranges National Park, established in 1995, lies about 107 km north-east of Melbourne and covers 76,003 hectares.
It has temperate rainforest and mountain ash, the tallest tree species in Australia, with specimens up to 80 metres.
Mount Donna Buang, at 1,245 m above Warburton, is the park's largest mountain.
Lady Talbot Drive is one of Victoria's most scenic drives, passing waterfalls, walks and flora.
Almost the whole park is a water catchment closed to visitors, and the open parts are popular day trips from Melbourne.

experiences: Walk among giant mountain ash
Drive scenic Lady Talbot Drive
Play in the snow at Mount Donna Buang

tips.title: Most of it is closed
tips.detail: Almost the entire park is water-catchment land closed to visitors, so stick to the open areas.

tips.title: Lake Mountain
tips.detail: Marysville, Lake Mountain and Cambarville offer skiing, bushwalking and mountain biking.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (drier months for forest drives; some roads close in winter).

name: Yarra Ranges National Park

facts.claim: Castlemaine is a gold-rush town of 7,506 people (2021) in the Goldfields, about 123 km north-west of Melbourne and 39 km from Bendigo.
It began as a gold boomtown in 1851 and is home to the Theatre Royal, the oldest continuously operating theatre in mainland Australia.
It has a vibrant arts scene popular with travellers from Melbourne.
A steam-run tourist railway operates from the station to nearby Maldon.
Trains from Melbourne run at least hourly and take about 90 minutes.

experiences: Explore goldfields arts and galleries
Ride the steam railway to Maldon
Step into goldfields history at Maldon

tips.title: Hourly trains
tips.detail: Trains from Melbourne run at least hourly and take about 90 minutes.

tips.title: Maldon steam train
tips.detail: A steam-run tourist railway runs from Castlemaine station to nearby Maldon.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement.

name: Castlemaine

facts.claim: Apollo Bay is a town on the Great Ocean Road between the Otway Ranges and the sea.
Cape Otway Lightstation, about 30 minutes away, is the oldest surviving lighthouse on the mainland and has operated since 1848.
Marriner's Lookout is a 30 minute return walk to a view of the town and coast.
Maits Rest is a 30 minute rainforest walk with a boardwalk and glow worms at night.
The Great Ocean Walk covers 104 km from Apollo Bay to the Twelve Apostles.
The road from Lorne to Apollo Bay was the last section finished, in 1932.

experiences: Walk Otway rainforest and glow-worm tracks
Visit Cape Otway's historic lighthouse
Start the Great Ocean Walk

tips.title: Faster inland
tips.detail: It is much faster to drive via Colac than along the Great Ocean Road, though the coast road is scenic.

tips.title: Marriner's Falls closed
tips.detail: The track to Marriner's Falls has been closed since 2011 because of falling trees.

tips.title: Great Ocean Walk
tips.detail: The 104 km Great Ocean Walk runs from Apollo Bay to the Twelve Apostles.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement (summer drive and walking season).

name: Apollo Bay

facts.claim: Wangaratta is a city of 29,808 (2021) in north-east Victoria, 236 km from Melbourne at the junction of the Ovens and King rivers.
It lies on the Hume Highway between Sydney and Melbourne, and NSW XPT services stop at the station.
The Murray to the Mountains rail trail starts here, with over 100 km of sealed off-road cycling.
Warby-Ovens National Park is about 10 minutes' drive away and is good for bushwalking.
The city has Art Deco buildings including the Courthouse.

experiences: Cycle the Murray to the Mountains rail trail
Walk the Warby Ranges

tips.title: Hot summers
tips.detail: The Warby Ranges can get very hot in summer, so walk earlier in the day or in cooler months.

tips.title: Train from Sydney
tips.detail: XPT services between Sydney and Melbourne stop in Wangaratta.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED judgement; the page warns the Warby Ranges get hot in summer.

name: Wangaratta
